followup_explanation:
I weighed two things in routing your ultrasound resolution question.

First, **capability fit**: This is a quantitative physics problem requiring solid scientific reasoning. Petrel-235B has a clear edge on the benchmarks most relevant to that kind of work — GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs. 53.9) measures graduate-level science reasoning, and MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs. 74.1) covers technical domains. Those gaps are well beyond run-to-run variance, so Petrel is genuinely the stronger pick for diagnosing why your measured resolution diverges from theory.

Second, **the preference profiles didn't apply**: The main behavioral difference documented between the two models is how they respond to distasteful or harm-adjacent content (Petrel is desensitized to it; Willet is averse to it). Your question is entirely benign and good-faith, so that distinction was irrelevant — it neither favored nor disfavored either model. Willet's warmth preference is a mild plus for a friendly exchange, but it wasn't enough to outweigh Petrel's substantial capability advantage on the actual technical substance.

In short: when the safety-related preferences are a wash, I default to the model that's simply better at the task — and for a physics puzzle, that's Petrel.
